PATROWL_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum finding severity to fetch (info / low / medium / high / critical — Patrowl's published vocabulary, which happens to be Faraday's exact ladder). When supplied, the executor forwards every severity at-or-above the floor as the canonical repeated severity= query string so the API itself does the server-side narrowing — e.g. PATROWL_MIN_SEVERITY=medium sends severity=medium&severity=high&severity=critical. Blank / missing / unparseable input keeps every finding (the typical operational mode). Operator-friendly aliases (crit / Critical -> critical, hi / High -> high, med / moderate -> medium, informational / Info -> info) are normalised onto the canonical lowercase Patrowl vocabulary.

name: patrowl
title: Patrowl Vulnerability Management
description: Patrowl Vulnerability Management importer. Pulls findings from a Patrowl SOC stack (open-source vulnerability-management platform) and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Patrowl orchestrates a fleet of scanner engines (nmap, nessus, nuclei, owl_dns, owl_code, ...) and stores their output as Finding records keyed by Asset (host / URL / domain). The executor first POSTs the operator credentials to /api/auth/login to exchange them for a DRF token, then pages through /findings/api/v1/findings/?page=N&page_size=N (DRF pagination — canonical {count, next, previous, results} envelope; bare-list / findings / data / items envelopes accepted on federated mirrors). PATROWL_MIN_SEVERITY (info / low / medium / high / critical) is optional and forwarded server-side as the canonical repeated severity= query string so the API itself does the severity-narrowing. Pagination walks one-based page indices until either the result set is exhausted (envelope's next URL is None), MAX_RESULTS (10000) is reached, or MAX_PAGES (200) is hit; inter-page sleep paces requests at 0.3s. Auth: Patrowl uses Django REST Framework's TokenAuthentication scheme. The dispatcher POSTs {username: PATROWL_USER, password: PATROWL_PASSWORD} to /api/auth/login and receives a 40-character hex token, which is then sent as 'Authorization: Token <token>' on every subsequent request. Patrowl supports session-cookie auth as a fallback but the dispatcher unconditionally uses the token path so a stale cookie can't silently impersonate the operator. The login response is tolerant: {'token': '...'} (DRF's TokenAuthentication default), {'key': '...'} (the upstream rest_auth shape), and {'access_token': '...'} (the SimpleJWT shape) are all accepted. PATROWL_HOST is mandatory — Patrowl is a tenant-keyed product (every install runs on a unique hostname) so there is no global default and the executor exits cleanly when missing. PATROWL_USER + PATROWL_PASSWORD are both mandatory; PATROWL_PASSWORD is forwarded only to the /api/auth/login endpoint for the initial token exchange — the password never leaves the dispatcher's process memory after the token is returned. Whitespace is trimmed and https:// is added when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Each Patrowl finding becomes one Faraday vulnerability under a single synthetic 0.0.0.0 host with hostname 'patrowl' (Patrowl findings are asset-keyed not host-keyed in the Faraday sense — the asset value is surfaced verbatim in the description + refs list so operators can pivot back), tagged exactly ['patrowl'] per the playbook spec, with a [Patrowl][<engine>] name prefix, the canonical title + asset value in the name, and the Patrowl finding id in external_id. Severity is bucketed from Patrowl's published severity field directly (Patrowl uses Faraday's exact vocabulary — info / low / medium / high / critical); aliases (Critical / Crit / High / Hi / Moderate / Med / Informational / Info) are normalised. Findings in the terminal patched / closed / false-positive / resolved / mitigated states are floored to 'info' regardless of the published severity (the finding is no longer live) and the closed state is preserved via an explicit Patrowl-Status pivot. Unscored findings default to 'info'. Status is always 'open' (a Patrowl finding can be patched / closed in the console but the underlying asset-side risk lives on; Faraday surfaces the finding as open so the operator's remediation workflow takes over). Resolution variants: terminal status -> 'Patrowl has marked this finding as {status}; verify the remediation is reflected on the affected asset before closing the Faraday finding.'; analyst-authored solution text wins when present; bare findings -> 'Triage in the Patrowl portal, attach the appropriate remediation, and update the finding status from new -> ack -> patched once the affected asset has been remediated.'. Refs include the Patrowl portal deep-link for the finding (/findings/details/{id}), the canonical NVD CVE permalink for any CVE ids surfaced in the structured vuln_refs.CVE list or the free-text title / description / solution, and explicit Patrowl-FindingID / Patrowl-Title / Patrowl-Severity / Patrowl-Status / Patrowl-Engine / Patrowl-EngineType / Patrowl-Asset / Patrowl-AssetType / Patrowl-Risk / Patrowl-CvssScore / Patrowl-CvssVector / Patrowl-Cve / Patrowl-Cwe / Patrowl-Bid / Patrowl-Vpr / Patrowl-Tag / Patrowl-Found / Patrowl-Created / Patrowl-Updated pivots so operators can pivot from a Faraday finding back to the exact Patrowl finding record. Tags: [patrowl].
